domain_setting: A calm home kitchen and neighborhood food market, with clean cutting boards, ceramic dishes, pantry shelves, and a seafood counter. Foods are presented fresh and appetizing without graphic slaughter or raw-food mess.
recurring_scale_anchors: 304x192 card with essential content inside x=24..280 and y=16..176
Use the same pale kitchen wall, warm wood counter, and ceramic plate language across the lesson
Food illustrations have clean silhouettes, a few tactile details, and generous clear space
Show separate items with distinct sizes, colors, cuts, or cooking methods rather than labels
No readable packaging, letters, numbers, brand marks, graphic raw meat, or unsafe food handling

polysemy_resolution_table.breast: A poultry cut in the meat-and-poultry food group, not human anatomy.
polysemy_resolution_table.chicken: Chicken as a food in this lesson's meat-and-poultry group; the provided Japanese gloss appears to describe a chick, so follow the food topic and neighboring cuts.
polysemy_resolution_table.leg: A poultry leg/drumstick cut in this food group, not a human or anatomical leg.
polysemy_resolution_table.cod: The edible cod fish in the fish-and-seafood group; the provided Japanese gloss appears to match an unrelated verb sense.
polysemy_resolution_table.dairy: Dairy foods and products such as milk, butter, and cheese, not a dairy farm or factory.
polysemy_resolution_table.cream (dairy): The thick dairy product poured or spooned into food; not the color cream.
polysemy_resolution_table.chips: Potato crisps in a bowl or packet, following the source form and U.S. snack usage; fries are a separate item.
polysemy_resolution_table.fries: Hot potato sticks served as a side, distinct from the thin, crisp snack called chips.
polysemy_resolution_table.nuts: Edible mixed nuts in the meal-and-snack group; not the informal adjective meaning crazy.
polysemy_resolution_table.shell: A hard shell from a sea animal, shown as an empty shell; not a general household shell or a whole seafood dish.
polysemy_resolution_table.seafood platter: A prepared serving of several kinds of seafood arranged together, distinct from the general category seafood.
polysemy_resolution_table.egg / eggs (plural): A whole raw hen's egg with its shell; cooked preparations appear in their own entries.
polysemy_resolution_table.egg white: The translucent uncooked albumen separated from yolk, shown without a shell.
polysemy_resolution_table.boiled egg: A hard-boiled egg cut open to show its firm yolk.
polysemy_resolution_table.fried egg: A single sunny-side-up egg cooked in a pan, with a set white and intact yolk.
polysemy_resolution_table.omelet: A folded cooked egg dish, distinct from a sunny-side-up egg or soft poached egg.
polysemy_resolution_table.poached egg: A softly cooked egg with a rounded white and hidden yolk, served without shell.
polysemy_resolution_table.scrambled eggs: Soft cooked curds of egg gathered together on a plate, distinct from an omelet.

contrast_notes.meat / beef / pork / lamb: Meat is the general category; beef is red meat; pork is shown as a pork chop; lamb is a smaller tender chop with a lamb cue.
contrast_notes.chicken / breast / leg: Chicken is a whole cooked bird; breast is a pale boneless fillet; leg is a recognizable drumstick.
contrast_notes.bacon / ham / sausages: Bacon is thin curled strips; ham is broad pink slices; sausages are plump linked cylinders.
contrast_notes.cod / mackerel / salmon / sardines: Cod is a pale whitefish; mackerel has dark wavy stripes; salmon has pink-orange flesh; sardines are several very small silvery fish.
contrast_notes.crab / lobster / prawn / shrimp: Crab has a broad body and sideways legs; lobster is large with prominent claws; prawn has a long curved body and long antennae; shrimp is smaller and tightly curled.
contrast_notes.mussel / oyster / scallops / shell: Mussels have narrow dark blue shells; oysters are irregular rough shells; scallops are fan-shaped ribbed shells; shell shows one empty shell on its own.
contrast_notes.cheese / cottage cheese / butter / marga: Cheese is a firm wedge; cottage cheese is small white curds; butter is a solid golden block; margarine is a soft spread in a shallow dish.
contrast_notes.boiled / fried / poached / scrambled egg: Give each cooked form its own utensil, shape, surface, and plating cue so the neighboring cards cannot be mistaken for one another.
contrast_notes.chips / fries: Chips are thin crisp rounds; fries are long golden potato sticks.
contrast_notes.fast food / burger / hot dog / fries: Fast food is a tray combining several quick-service items; the other cards focus on one named food.
